title: Danmu Jingao Tablet attenuates periodontitis by promoting SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation and mitochondrial redox homeostasis.
byline: Liu H, Wang Y, Yu Y, et al.
html:
Ethnopharmacological relevance: Nauclea officinalis (Pierre ex Pit.) Merr. & Chun is a traditional medicinal plant widely used by the Li ethnic group in Hainan Province, China. Danmu Jingao Tablet (DMJGT), a Chinese patent medicine derived from this plant, exhibits well-documented anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which macrophage oxidative stress and M1 polarization are key drivers. However, whether DMJGT exerts its anti-periodontitis effects through regulating macrophage polarization remains unclear.

Aim of the study: This study aimed to investigate whether DMJGT ameliorates periodontitis by upregulating SIRT3 expression and enhancing the SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation pathway, thereby suppressing macrophage oxidative stress, preserving mitochondrial function, and modulating macrophage polarization.

Materials and methods: DMJGT constituents were analyzed by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS, with molecular docking, MD simulations, and SPR predicting compound-SIRT3 binding. In ligature-induced periodontitis mice, alveolar bone loss and histopathology were evaluated by Micro-CT and staining. In LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, ROS, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress markers, protein levels (SIRT3, SOD2, Ac-SOD2, TFAM, PGC-1α, CD86, CD206), and mRNA (Sirt3, Il1b, Il6, Tnf) were assessed. SIRT3 dependency was confirmed by 3-TYP inhibition in vivo and siRNA knockdown in vitro.

Results: Eighty-three compounds were identified, with strictosamide, vincosamide, and naucleofficine A showing high binding affinity to SIRT3. DMJGT reduced alveolar bone loss, osteoclasts, and inflammation. It upregulated SIRT3, TFAM, and PGC-1α, decreased Ac-SOD2 (K68), restored redox markers, suppressed M1 and promoted M2 polarization, and reduced cytokines. 3-TYP or Sirt3 siRNA reversed these effects.

Conclusions: DMJGT alleviates periodontitis by upregulating SIRT3 expression and enhancing the SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation pathway. This pathway reduces oxidative stress, preserves mitochondrial function, and reprograms macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. SIRT3 is a critical target for DMJGT, providing a new mechanistic basis for its clinical application in periodontitis.
